papers.title: Biomechanical Comparison of Titanium and CFR-PEEK Intramedullary Nails Using Finite Element Analysis
papers.abstract: This study analyzes the biomechanical performance of intramedullary nails made of titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) and carbon fiber-reinforced polyetheretherketone (CFR-PEEK) for the treatment of proximal femoral fractures, with a focus on their effects under different bone density conditions representing young and osteoporotic bone. Using finite element models and analyses simulating mid-stance gait loading and incorporating muscle forces adjusted for age-related reduction, the load transfer and stress distribution were evaluated, along with the osteogenic index (OI) as a measure of biological stimulus for bone healing. Results showed that titanium nails produced lower bone stresses but caused significant proximal stress shielding, particularly in osteoporotic bone, which could impair healing. In contrast, CFR-PEEK nails exhibited higher and more uniformly distributed stresses along the femoral diaphysis and shifted the osteogenic stimulus into a range promoting more mature bone formation in both young and elderly femora. The composite material’s elastic modulus closer to bone and its orthotropic fiber arrangement contributed to these effects. The study concludes that CFR-PEEK nails offer a promising alternative to titanium by reducing stress shielding and enhancing the biomechanical environment favorable for fracture healing, especially in osteoporotic patients. Future work will include dynamic loading conditions and experimental validation to optimize implant design.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及股骨髓内钉而非髋关节股骨柄，与Ti-6Al-4V股骨柄结构设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on intramedullary nails for fracture fixation, not femoral/hip stem implants for arthroplasty, and lacks the structural design, lattice architecture, or stem fatigue analysis required for this direction.

summary_zh.validation: 仅有有限元分析，无实验验证

summary_en.motivation: This study compares the biomechanical performance of titanium alloy and CFR-PEEK intramedullary nails for proximal femoral fracture fixation.
summary_en.method: Finite element models with mid-stance gait loading and muscle forces were used to evaluate stress distribution and osteogenic index.
summary_en.result: CFR-PEEK nails reduced stress shielding and promoted a more favorable biomechanical environment for bone healing compared to titanium nails.
summary_en.validation: The study relies solely on finite element analysis without experimental validation.

papers.title: In situ tailoring of Ti6Al4V microstructure via laser powder bed fusion with secondary laser processing
papers.venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology

llm.relevance_to_user: 对于Ti-6Al-4V增材制造工艺改进有参考价值，但缺乏力学性能表征。
llm.why_not_core: No explicit mechanical or fatigue characterization reported; focus is on microstructural tailoring via secondary laser processing, not on mechanical performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过二次激光加工原位调控Ti6Al4V微观结构
summary_zh.method: 采用激光粉末床熔融结合二次激光处理

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to tailor the microstructure of Ti6Al4V in situ during laser powder bed fusion by employing a secondary laser processing step.
summary_en.method: A secondary laser is applied concurrently with the main laser in LPBF to modify thermal history and resultant microstructure.
summary_en.result: The approach demonstrates the ability to produce graded or customized microstructures in Ti6Al4V components.
summary_en.validation: No mechanical or fatigue testing is reported; validation is limited to microstructural characterization.

papers.title: Fatigue performance analysis of dental implants: Influence of thread design
papers.abstract: This study investigates the fatigue performance of dental implants made from titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V), with a focus on the influence of thread geometry on fatigue resistance. Two implant models with distinct thread profiles are considered: triangular and trapezoidal. The implants were designed using CAD software and analyzed via finite element analysis (FEA) by ANSYS. A fixed part was considered to simulate the surrounding bone, and a force of 118.2 N was applied according to ISO 14801 dental standard [1]. The results of static analysis reveal that the triangular thread design is subjected to the high peak stress of 290MPa localized at the thread edges, which could be a potential site of fatigue failure. In contrast, the trapezoidal thread design demonstrates lower level of stress distribution, with a reduced of the maximum stress concentrations of 216MPa. Fatigue analysis shows that the trapezoidal threaded implant offers significantly better performance, with a minimum lifespan approximately 4.7 times higher than the triangular threaded implant. The obtained result could be attributed to its larger contact surface and optimized load distribution compared to the triangular thread geometry. These findings highlight the importance of thread geometry in enhancing the mechanical reliability and longevity of dental implants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及增材制造工艺，与用户关注的方向不匹配。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not mention additive manufacturing; it is a general FEA study on dental implant thread design without any AM context.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究螺纹几何形状对Ti-6Al-4V牙种植体疲劳性能的影响
summary_zh.method: 通过CAD设计两种螺纹模型，利用ANSYS有限元分析模拟静态和疲劳载荷
summary_zh.result: 梯形螺纹设计应力集中更低，疲劳寿命约为三角形螺纹的4.7倍
summary_zh.validation: 仅有限元模拟，无实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the influence of thread geometry on the fatigue performance of Ti-6Al-4V dental implants.
summary_en.method: Two implant models with triangular and trapezoidal thread profiles were designed and analyzed using finite element analysis (ANSYS) under ISO 14801 loading conditions.
summary_en.result: The trapezoidal thread design exhibited lower peak stress (216 MPa vs 290 MPa) and approximately 4.7 times higher fatigue life than the triangular design.
summary_en.validation: The study relied solely on finite element simulation without experimental validation.
